A bigger, more useful CPU widget, smooth memory graphs, cleaner traffic lanes on the Network Map, the connections behind every country on the Traffic Map, a new logo, and self-repair after OPNsense firmware updates.

### Dashboard

- **CPU widget**:
  - The graph is 132 px tall instead of 50, so changes are easy to read.
  - It now shows the load in large type, User / System / Interrupt, a one-minute average and the CPU temperature (average of the cores; the hottest core is in the tooltip). The load turns amber or red when it runs high.
  - It all comes from the widget's own live stream; only the temperature is read separately, every 15 seconds.
- **Memory and the other meters scroll smoothly**. The graph now moves continuously, like the CPU graph, with one linear slide per update, instead of jumping each time. The spacing stays fixed and the scale changes only when the values leave it, so the line no longer jumps or squeezes.

### Network Map

- **Two lanes per busy link**. A link that carries traffic turns into a soft cable with two strings: download as blue streaks towards the devices, upload as green dashes back to the firewall. They replace the row of crowded dots, and both lanes run parallel along the curves.
- Idle links stay a thin grey line.

### Traffic Map: connections

- **See the connections behind a country**. Open a country's row and choose *Show the connections*, or click a country in *All countries*. Clicking the *Connections* card shows every connection. Each line shows:
  - the **device** on your network, with its Network Map name or hostname and its address;
  - the **remote address and port**;
  - the **service**: HTTPS, DNS, NTP, Steam, STUN, WireGuard, …;
  - the **network** it belongs to, with its AS number;
  - the **live download/upload**, the **data transferred** so far, and how long it has been **open**.
- The busiest 300 connections are listed. Type to filter by device, address, service or network. The list refreshes with the page.

### New logo

The node mark: a "U" whose two ends are network nodes, linked to a centre node. It is used in the sidebar, on the sign-in page and as the browser icon.

### Safe across firmware updates

- OPNsense updates leave UniSense's files alone. The installer now also adds a self-check that OPNsense runs **after every firmware update and at every boot** (`rc.syshook.d/update` and `start`).
- It compares every installed file with the installer's list. Anything missing or empty is restored from a copy of the same release kept in `/var/db/unisense/keep`.
- It then clears the menu cache so the Lobby pages appear under the new core.
- It never changes your selected theme or your cron jobs, and does nothing when all is in place. `sh install.sh --status` shows "Self-repair".
- The installer no longer copies stray Python caches (`__pycache__`).

### README

The README now has badges for the release, download count, stars and build status, sections for the Traffic Map and connections, and an FAQ entry on firmware updates.

### Update

```sh
fetch -o - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ox1d3x3/unisense/main/install.sh | sh
```

Reload the page in your browser (Ctrl+F5) to pick up the new styles and logo.
